cu-001.label: Analyze an invoice PDF and read the extracted vendor, total and due-date fields
cu-001.why: prebuilt-invoice extracts structured fields from invoice documents — the exam's most-tested prebuilt analyzer (7 mentions).

cu-002.label: Define your own field schema in natural language and extract those fields from contracts
cu-002.why: Custom analyzers are built from a field schema you describe — CU's plain-language field description is what separates it from Document Intelligence prebuilts.

cu-003.label: Extract text and identified objects from photographed equipment labels
cu-003.why: prebuilt-image extracts text and objects from still images through the same analyzer workflow as every other modality.

cu-004.label: Get a transcript plus summary and speaker breakdown from recorded support calls
cu-004.why: CU's audio analyzers return transcripts, summaries and speakers — extraction, never speech synthesis.

cu-005.label: Segment recorded training sessions and index their transcripts and visual events for search
cu-005.why: Video analyzers return segments, transcripts and visual events; the *Search variants prepare content for retrieval — Azure AI Search indexes what CU extracts.

cu-006.label: Return text, tables, and selection marks with document structure — no field semantics
cu-006.why: Layout extracts text, tables, selection marks and structure; Read-style OCR is text only — histack's CU Read-vs-Layout distinction.

cu-007.label: A mixed batch of vendor forms needs their loose key-value pairs pulled out without starting from a predefined field schema
cu-007.why: prebuilt-documentFields extracts general key-value pairs from documents with no domain-specific schema required — unlike prebuilt-invoice's fixed invoice fields.

cu-008.label: Before building a custom analyzer for a brand-new form type, ask Content Understanding to propose the field schema, then base the new analyzer on the general document analyzer
cu-008.why: prebuilt-documentFieldSchema proposes fields for a document type you haven't schema'd yet; prebuilt-document is the base_analyzer_id used when defining a new custom document analyzer — two distinct ids in the same custom-build workflow.

cu-009.label: Run the Python quickstart against a product photo and read the generated description back from the result's Summary field
cu-009.why: prebuilt-imageSearch is the quickstart analyzer for descriptive image output — its result exposes a Summary field holding the natural-language description.

cu-010.label: Build a custom analyzer that pulls a chart's Title and ChartType fields out of a batch of dashboard screenshots
cu-010.why: Custom image analyzers set base_analyzer_id to prebuilt-image before layering a field schema — the documented pattern for chart and screenshot extraction.

cu-011.label: Analyze shelf photos from a retail audit and return structured fields for product count, brand presence, and out-of-stock indicators
cu-011.why: Content Understanding's image analyzer returns schema-defined structured fields straight from photos — the retail shelf-audit scenario the exam tests directly.

cu-012.label: Wire a Python client that calls begin_analyze with analyzer_id="prebuilt-image" against a photo URL, then read back the detected objects from the result
cu-012.why: The begin_analyze(analyzer_id=..., inputs=[AnalysisInput(url=...)]) call pattern is identical across modalities — only the analyzer id changes, and prebuilt-image is the direct (non-search) image analyzer.

cu-013.label: Wire a lightweight Python client that calls begin_analyze with a call-recording URL to pull back a transcript and summary ready for a retrieval index
cu-013.why: prebuilt-audioSearch is the documented analyzer id in the SDK's quickstart snippet — the *Search suffix marks output prepped for indexing/RAG retrieval, unlike prebuilt-audio's direct extraction with no retrieval prep.

cu-014.label: Pull speaker-labeled, precisely timed transcript phrases out of a batch of podcast episodes
cu-014.why: transcriptPhrases is the output field carrying speaker identification and timing information — a direct audio-extraction output, distinct from the analyzer id itself.

cu-015.label: Recognize that submitting a podcast MP3 to Content Understanding sets the contents object's kind to the same value used for video inputs
cu-015.why: Audio-only and video inputs both use kind: "audioVisual" in the contents schema — a shared value that trips up anyone expecting a distinct 'audio' kind.

cu-016.label: Confirm that pulling a structured transcript out of a voicemail inbox is speech captured into text, never text turned into speech
cu-016.why: CU's audio analyzers transcribe existing speech into structured output — they never synthesize new spoken output; that job belongs to Azure AI Speech, not Content Understanding.

cu-017.label: Divide an uploaded recorded product demo into logical scene segments before any downstream processing runs
cu-017.why: enableSegment is the analyzer schema property that splits footage into logical segments such as scenes — a video-analyzer control, not an audio or document one.

cu-018.label: After analyzing a marketing clip, read back a structured markdown summary of its transcript and visual content
cu-018.why: prebuilt-videoSearch results expose a markdown field summarizing transcript and visual content per segment — the SDK's documented read-back field for video.

cu-019.label: Confirm that extracting keyframes and visual events from an uploaded recording works on footage that already exists, rather than generating new frames
cu-019.why: CU's analyzers extract keyframes, transcripts and visual events from footage that already exists — they don't generate synthetic frames; that's a different category of AI service entirely.

cu-020.label: Wire a Python client that calls begin_analyze with analyzer_id="prebuilt-videoSearch" against an uploaded MP4 URL
cu-020.why: The begin_analyze(analyzer_id="prebuilt-videoSearch", inputs=[AnalysisInput(url=...)]) call is the documented SDK pattern for kicking off video extraction.

cu-modality-grid.hint: Ask what the source file actually is, then check the sub line for the exact prebuilt-* analyzer id — the id itself names its modality (document/image/audio/video), and Search-suffixed ids prep output for indexing rather than change the modality.
cu-modality-grid.note: Content Understanding always extracts — it never generates or indexes. Extraction into Azure AI Search is a downstream step, not something CU does itself.
cu-modality-grid.zones[0].def: PDFs, invoices, contracts and freeform paperwork Content Understanding turns into structured fields, tables and text.
cu-modality-grid.zones[1].def: Photos, screenshots and charts Content Understanding turns into structured fields, descriptions and detected objects.
cu-modality-grid.zones[2].def: Recorded speech — calls, podcasts and voicemails — Content Understanding turns into transcripts, summaries and speaker labels.
cu-modality-grid.zones[3].def: Recorded footage Content Understanding segments, transcribes and prepares for search.
